request: Sodium-ion battery anode composite combining hard carbon with carbon black conductive additive and sodium-compatible binder (CMC/SBR). The material targets: (1) specific capacity >300 mAh/g at C/10 rate, (2) excellent rate capability to 2C, (3) coulombic efficiency >98% for 100 cycles, (4) low volume expansion <20%, and (5) electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis to track SEI formation and stability.

Lithium-ion battery cathode composite: LiCoO₂ blended with nickel oxide and manganese oxide to enhance cycling stability and lower cobalt content. Half-cell testing targets: (1) discharge capacity >180 mAh/g at C/20, (2) capacity retention >80% after 200 cycles, (3) safe operation to 4.5V vs Li/Li+, and (4) electrochemical impedance tracking to assess structural stability.

Silicon-based anode composite for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries. Silicon nanoparticles are embedded in carbon matrix with optimized binder formulation to manage volume expansion. Electrochemical testing: (1) initial capacity 2500+ mAh/g, (2) stable capacity >1200 mAh/g after 100 cycles, (3) coulombic efficiency >95%, and (4) galvanostatic charge-discharge at multiple rates (C/20 to 2C).

Solid-state battery anode: metallic lithium or sodium metal deposited on current collector with ceramic electrolyte. Key metrics: (1) electrochemical stability up to 5.0V, (2) reversible plating/stripping for 500+ cycles without dendrite, (3) galvanostatic testing at increasing current densities (0.5-10 mA/cm²), and (4) EIS characterization of solid electrolyte interface (SEI).

Potassium-ion battery anode material based on graphite or metal oxide. The anode shows: (1) reversible K+ intercalation capacity >200 mAh/g, (2) lower voltage window compared to lithium (0.5-2.5V vs K+/K), (3) excellent cycle life 500+ cycles, and (4) electrochemical impedance revealing ion transport kinetics and electrode interface stability.

Dual-carbon battery anode-cathode system: activated carbon or hard carbon for both terminals, avoiding materials scarcity. Performance targets: (1) cell voltage 1.0-2.0V (asymmetric configuration), (2) energy density 50-100 Wh/kg, (3) cycle life >1000 cycles, (4) high rate capability (10C discharge), and (5) low-cost manufacturing compatible with mass production.

Electrolyte additive material for lithium-ion battery to improve cycling stability and suppress dendrite formation. Additives tested: (1) lithium nitrate (LiNO₃), (2) phosphorus pentoxide compounds, (3) silicon-containing salts. Electrochemical evaluation includes galvanostatic charge-discharge curves, coulombic efficiency, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and extended cycling (500+ cycles).

Zinc-air battery anode: porous zinc foam or zinc powder composite that enables high capacity utilization with reversible electrochemistry. Testing: (1) galvanostatic discharge to 0.6V cutoff, (2) reversible charging with appropriate catalyst/electrolyte, (3) cycle life assessment 100-500 cycles, (4) energy efficiency >60% (discharge/charge voltage ratio), and (5) safety testing for thermal runaway prevention.
